features.feature: Proof-or-stop requires mechanical host availability evidence before accepting degraded single-host fallback.
Expose review_host_availability_probe so users can see a probe id, materialHash, and canonical rows for codex, claude, and agy.
Persist probe evidence as local process evidence bound to current material state, with host rows, availableHostCount, and process-fact registry coverage.
Probe implementation must derive host availability internally and must not accept caller-supplied host status as proof.
Unavailable canonical hosts are represented as unavailable rows with path/version/error details instead of being omitted.
single-host-environment and temporary-host-unavailability fallback records require fresh probe evidence and reject when two or more canonical hosts are available.
review_escalation_status and review assurance floor evaluators mark missing, stale, contradictory, legacy, or manually injected fallback evidence invalid.
explicit-human-approval remains available only as visible degraded-single-host lower assurance with approvalRef or evidence and never full 3x2 or Authority completion.
Smoke tests and diagnostics cover missing probe, two available hosts, insufficient hosts, explicit human approval, and recovery guidance.
Gate-consumed host proof facts are registered in process-fact levels, process-fact registry, command policy, and verify-process-fact-contract coverage.
Do not redesign or implement the full cross-host review runner or broader Tier-C collection mechanism.
features.excluded_by: Story background and decision choose a narrow host availability evidence path, not a runner redesign.

features.feature: Do not create Authority, production, remote release, or cryptographic Tier-C proof from this local host availability diagnostic.
features.excluded_by: Related decisions keep local diagnostic and local review quorum evidence non-Authority and non-production.

features.feature: Do not change ordinary review escalation triggers or force every story through 3x2.
features.excluded_by: Related review escalation policy keeps existing first-review-round trigger and this story only hardens degraded fallback admissibility.

features.feature: Temporary host unavailability for an executable host with auth, quota, outage, or rate-limit failure has an ambiguous coverage boundary under the proposed path/version probe.

openQuestions.q: For CHK-001 and CHK-002, should available mean executable and version-responsive only, or review-capable including auth, quota, outage, and rate-limit readiness for temporary-host-unavailability?
openQuestions.evidence: The plan says the probe checks codex, claude, and agy command lookup/version and rejects when two or more canonical hosts are executable, while the related review escalation decision allows temporary-host-unavailability when a second host was attempted or probed and unavailable because of credits, auth, runtime, outage, or rate limits. This predicate affects the probe schema, fallback validator, and smoke tests before DEV.
